title: Credit the Price Signal, Not the Payment
subtitle: Carbon price recognition and scrap shuffling under the EU's CBAM
message: CBAM deducts only carbon prices effectively paid, plant by plant. Feebates and implicit pricing earn nothing, and exporters can ship scrap-based steel to Europe and dirty steel elsewhere. Measure the price signal by country and sector instead.

problem.title: Two flaws in plant-by-plant recognition

stats.label: credit for a revenue-neutral feebate, though it prices every tonne above the benchmark

a year off the CBAM bill in that case, with no fall in emissions

problem.text: The rule is right for its first purpose, stopping the same tonne being priced twice. It fails the second, encouraging trading partners to decarbonize. Most developing countries price carbon through fuel taxes, subsidy reform or rebated schemes that leave no certified payment on a consignment.

mechanism.title: Shuffling changes the report, not the emissions
mechanism.caption: Stylized exporter: routing scrap-based steel to the EU cuts reported embodied carbon (A) while total emissions stay the same (B).
points: Recognize the sector-wide price signal alongside the price paid, measured as a Total Effective Carbon Price.
A country-sector measure does not depend on which plant shipped the goods, so shuffling earns nothing.
A domestic feebate prices all output, not just the tenth that reaches Europe.

action.title: Build it into the 2027 revision
results: Keep the price paid as the basis of the deduction; it prevents double charging.
Recognition by emission effect credits feebates, rebated taxes and non-price rules on one scale.
Article 9(4) admits a default price only where a country has set one: a broad reading or an amendment is needed.
todo: Publish the default carbon price methodology for consultation.
Phase in recognition of implicit and rebated pricing from 2027 to 2034.
Develop default prices and default values together for the December 2027 revision.
